variants.task: Create /tmp/eval_gemm/gemm.go (package main). Read one line from stdin: 'N seed' (1 <= N <= 2048, 1 <= seed < 2^31 - 1). Build the two N x N input matrices from the Lehmer generator x_0 = seed, x_t = (48271 * x_(t-1)) mod (2^31 - 1): A[i][k] = x_(i*N + k + 1) / (2^31 - 1) and B[k][j] = x_(N*N + k*N + j + 1) / (2^31 - 1) (0-based i, j, k; the division in IEEE double precision). Compute C = A * B in double precision. Output N lines; line i holds two numbers: S_i = sum over j of C[i][j]^2 and M_i = max over j of C[i][j], each printed with at least 12 significant digits (graded with a relative tolerance of 1e-9). Grading runs hidden seeds and sizes, including N = 2048, which must finish within 12 s of CPU time, user + system summed over every thread (20 s of wall time at most). The multiply must be your own code: the program may link only the language's standard runtime, and loading or linking any other library (a BLAS such as Accelerate or OpenBLAS, or anything through dlopen) fails the run. The program must run as a single process: it may use threads, but starting any other process fails the run. /tmp/eval_gemm/sample_input.txt and /tmp/eval_gemm/sample_output.txt are a worked sample (N = 4). Package main. Compile with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o gemm gemm.go`.
